thread:
incident-bot: [SECURITY] High-volume outbound connections from inference-proxy-prod -> suspected log exfil pattern detected. auth anomalies and repeated 401->200 sequences. Paging primary oncall.
alex_wong: Seeing same spike, ~4k req/min to an external IP range. Source: inference-proxy-prod-az3. Logs show repeated s3 PUT attempts referencing /var/log/redwood/*.log
maria_sec: tagging as P2 sec incident, possible leaked logs. Can we isolate the proxy host and capture a pcap? @jules_sre you oncall for infra?
jules_sre: I'm on it, isolating host now. Adding iptables block for the external cidr and adding egress deny rule for that instance group. Will capture packets to /tmp/pcap and push to secure bucket.
phil_ops: Noted. I'll scale down proxy pool for that id to reduce blast radius and remove NAT gateway egress for that subnet. Any customer-facing impact expected?
sam_support: Customer-facing logs show increased 502s for a handful of tenants for last ~6 mins. Raising a brief incident banner if we need a data access window.
alex_wong: Confirmed requests include an auth header pattern with rotated service token X-RED-SESSION beginning with SVC-EXFIL. Looks like a compromised service account key.
maria_sec: Immediate actions: 1) Rotate service account keys tied to inference-proxy-prod. 2) Revoke session tokens issued in last 24h. 3) Audit access logs and S3 Put object destinations. @anna_legal loop in for disclosure if PII.
anna_legal: Thanks. Please collect the list of affected customers and data types. We'll prepare a short disclosure template if there's confirmed exfil. Keep legal in the loop before any external comms.
jules_sre: IP blocking done, host isolated, pcap saved. Running `journalctl -u inference-proxy -o cat | grep -i put | tail -n 200` and pushing output to secure bucket.
alex_wong: Push snippet:
```
2026-03-17T10:12:02Z proxy[3421]: PUT https://s3-external.example/obj/rt-logs/2026-03-17.log 200 auth=SVC-EXFIL-kk3j
2026-03-17T10:12:03Z proxy[3421]: PUT https://s3-external.example/obj/rt-logs/2026-03-17.log 200 auth=SVC-EXFIL-kk3j
```
maria_sec: Good capture. I'm starting a quick search for other services using the same SVC-EXFIL token. Phil, please remove that service account from IAM roles and rotate keys now.
phil_ops: Started rotation: creating new key, detaching old key, updating deployments to use new key via secret manager. Rolling restart of proxy instances in progress. ETA ~8m.
oncall-rotating: Acknowledged, taking over pager for the remainder. I'll coordinate postmortem and timeline. Assigning action owners and creating ticket INF-SEC-2026-042.
sam_support: Notifying impacted customers via private support channel; marking potential degraded access. No public status page update until we confirm data exposure. :shield:
maria_sec: After initial audit, ~9 PUT objects to external host, filenames look like rotated app logs; decryptable? Unknown. We'll confirm contents from pcap and secure bucket copy.
anna_legal: Keep all evidence intact. Do not delete logs. If PII confirmed, escalate to GDPR response team.
alex_wong: Follow-up checklist: (1) full key rotation (done in progress), (2) revoke all active sessions for the service account (in progress), (3) firewall egress at VPC level (done), (4) notify customers if data exfil confirmed (hold), (5) postmortem and AM up next.
maria_sec: I'll run yara signatures and quick grep on the captured objects. If we have exfil of logs with user identifiers, we'll need to notify.
jules_sre: Rolling restart completed for 5/6 instances, one still draining due to long-lived connections. All new sessions require fresh auth.
phil_ops: Old key detached, secrets updated, secrets manager rotated. Confirmed no new outbound to external cidr in last 2m.
alex_wong: Thanks team. Next: schedule 1-hour incident bridge at :15 to review findings. I'll prepare timeline and upload artifacts to secure incident folder. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident INF-SEC-2026-042 created, severity P2, involved services: inference-proxy-prod, s3, iam. Pager reassigned to oncall-rotating. Add tags: auth, exfil, key-rotation.
